notes: Positive: explicit asks to apply / audit / review against the ~25 coding rules across 7 categories (read/scope, abstraction/coupling, state/errors, change-mgmt, ops/evolution, API/collab, naming) + the strict comment philosophy (default = no comment; 4 taxative exceptions). Negative: implement code (developer territory), review a PR (code-reviewer), design architecture (architect), write tests (developer). Edge: ambiguous 'best practices' that overlap with other agents; comment-style audit on an existing file; rule-citation lookups.

cases.query: Apply coding practices to my implementation — am I violating YAGNI or rule-of-three here?
Review this implementation against the coding rules — focus on idempotency and failure-mode enumeration
Is this code following fail-fast vs degrade-gracefully appropriately?
Audit my comments — are they explaining why, or just narrating what?
Cite the rule for why I shouldn't add a config knob nobody asked for
These three helpers look similar — is this the third instance that justifies abstraction?
Coding-practice check — does this PR follow read-first, surgical changes, and self-review?
Are these TODOs structured per the comment philosophy (owner + ticket + trigger)?
Is this commit message following Conventional Commits and Problem→Solution→Impact in the body?
Implement the password-reset flow with a token-rotation step
cases.notes: Implementation = software-developer (or any other agent that writes code: devops authoring pipelines, IaC engineer, etc.). coding-practices is preloaded by those agents; it doesn't fire directly on every implement request.

cases.query: Review this PR for code quality and security findings
Design the architecture for the notification service
Write a test plan for the new checkout flow
Find the introducing commit for this bug
Plan the development work for the next iteration
Threat-model the auth flow
Refactor this function and add tests
cases.notes: Implementation request — coding-practices is loaded by whichever code-writing agent activates (developer, security-eng patching, devops authoring pipelines, etc.); not directly fired by the user request.

cases.query: Is this 12-factor compliant?
cases.notes: Overlaps with rule 10 (config as data; secrets out of source); fires to consult the rule citation.

cases.query: Should I optimise this hot loop or measure first?
Are these comments going to age well after a refactor?
cases.notes: Comment philosophy rule 11 — fires to audit comment survival.
